variables.name: sOther
variables.meaning: all unchanged canonical Tabular slice cardinality

contract.proof: Each DataTable event and controlled synchronization dispatches to exactly one owner-local canonicalizer; unchanged canonical slices are reused by identity and are not traversed.
contract.adversarialWitness: A one-ID expansion update beside maximum-size canonical query, selection, and column slices visits the expansion only.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary slice updates may validate their external slice but cannot rescan unrelated canonical state.

contract.proof: The current projection generation retains row, column, and cell indexes; a valid adjacent move performs O(1) coordinate lookup and scans only candidates on its movement axis.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every candidate on a 100k-row axis is disabled, forcing one bounded axis scan without rebuilding cell records or indexes.

fullScan.rationale: Canonical movement is bounded to one axis; whole-domain recovery is a separate reconciliation fallback.

contract.proof: Column partitions and one projected index are built once; each header node contributes to one descendant interval exactly once.
contract.adversarialWitness: A maximum-depth header tree with hidden and pinned leaves is visited once and rejects the first non-contiguous group without per-group column scans.

fullScan.rationale: An external column-state replacement must establish the complete header topology invariant once.

contract.proof: Cold normalization/filter/group/projection are linear and comparator sorting dominates at n log n before access slicing.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every record passes filters and reverse-order sort requires comparison work before a one-row window.

fullScan.rationale: Cold resolution must inspect the external snapshot before producing the first query index.

contract.proof: A source generation rebuilds normalization plus query stages; a query revision reuses normalized identities but rebuilds filtering, grouping, pivot discovery, and sorting before slicing.
contract.adversarialWitness: Alternating query revisions over a reverse-ordered 100k-record source rebuild and sort the current query stage on every resolve.

fullScan.rationale: Changed source or query semantics require inspecting the affected current-stage input.

contract.proof: Equal source, query, and expansion revisions reuse the single retained projection; resolve validates the envelope and slices only the requested output window.
contract.adversarialWitness: A 100k-record retained projection returns a 100-row window without invoking identity, filter, sort, group, pivot, aggregate, or full-projection work.

fullScan.rationale: Warm resolution is output-sensitive and cannot rescan the retained source or projection.

contract.proof: Table lookup delegates to the Core Sequence index. Grid lookup combines retained row and column indexes into a row-major coordinate.
contract.adversarialWitness: Repeated last-row and last-column lookup on a large projection performs no Array.indexOf call and retains no cell-ID map.

fullScan.rationale: Locator calls are hot-path identity lookups and must not scan rows, columns, or cells.

variables.name: nRow
variables.meaning: current and next projected row cardinality

variables.name: j
variables.meaning: identity edits required by the bounded sparse repair

contract.proof: A fixed 32-patch planner bounds incremental array and persistent-layout work. Larger diffs use one splice, reuse stable-ID extents from the current indexed domain, and call the extent policy only for new IDs.
contract.adversarialWitness: Reverse order, a large filter, and mixed insertion/removal at 100k rows each produce one bulk mutation; a pure rotation produces one move mutation.

fullScan.rationale: Reconciliation must compare the next identity domain once; it cannot repeatedly scan it per unbounded edit.
